title: ARPAPED Agent Cycle Report
description: Machine-readable report of one completed cycle (blueprint/1-CYCLE.md, Phase 0-9). The counterpart to agent-cycle-input.schema.json: that schema defines what goes into a cycle, this one defines what comes out. Written into the resulting state alongside the verification record it references.

goal.description: The goal accepted at bootstrap, after the ecosystem was resolved.

starting_state.description: The current_state the cycle began from.

reusable_discovery.description: References to canonical implementations resolved (Bridge, Registry, Policy, Selector, assembler, existing capabilities) — Phase 1/3.

decisions.description: One entry per responsibility decomposed in Phase 2, decided in Phase 4.

failure.description: What broke while pursuing this responsibility's decision, if anything -- scoped to exactly this responsibility, never a cycle-wide narrative. 'summary' is the short, greppable label (an error code, a check_id); 'detail' is the fuller account. Optional: most decisions in a green cycle carry neither this nor 'correction'.

correction.description: What fixed the stated 'failure', if it was fixed within this same cycle. Requires 'failure' to be present too (dependentRequired below) -- a correction with nothing on record to correct is not a correction. The reverse is NOT required: a 'failure' with no 'correction' is a real, valid outcome (verification.status ended 'failed' and the cycle stopped before a fix landed) -- exactly the unresolved-failure signal a future learning agent needs, not something the schema should force into a fabricated correction just to validate.

check_ids.description: check_id(s), from this cycle's own verification-record.json, that exercised this responsibility's capability operation(s) -- the explicit link blueprint.dep.dataset_builder needs to fold a check's selection/evidence/trace onto this decision's row without guessing by string-matching responsibility against description (2-RULES.md "No silent defaults on what resolution depends on" applies here too). Optional -- absent for a decision with no directly-testable operation (e.g. a split/refactor decision).

reused_capabilities.description: Capability ids reused from a prior cycle, unchanged.

split_refactor_operations.description: Lineage references for any component split this cycle (Phase 1.5, Phase 8 Gate 8).

registry_changes.description: What was assembled/registered into the canonical Registry this cycle (Phase 8).

bridge_integration.description: Confirmation that every request traverses the canonical path through the single request-construction point (R6).

verification.description: Report against the checklist in blueprint/2-RULES.md ("Verification contract").

harness.description: Path/identity of the verification harness in the resulting state.

trace_evaluation.description: Summary of observed Bridge traces for every capability operation.

failures_and_fixes.description: Failures observed and fixes applied; regression re-run status. Should roll up / summarize the structured failure/correction pairs recorded in decisions[], when any exist; may also record failures that don't map to one specific decision (harness infrastructure flakiness, an ecosystem-resolution ambiguity). The structured per-decision fields are the primary record for anything decision-scoped -- this field is the overflow, not the only place a failure can be recorded.

verification_record_ref.description: Path to the verification-record.schema.json instance this cycle produced.

resulting_state.description: The authoritative discoverable state this cycle produced — the next cycle's current_state.

content_hash.description: sha256 over resulting_state's own relevant files' bytes (blueprint.dep.state_ref), sorted for determinism -- an immutable identifier that never depends on git, always computable, always present when this object exists at all.

vcs.description: OPTIONAL supplementary git identity, present only when resulting_state actually lived in a git working tree at capture time -- never required; DEP's own historical-reconstruction story stands on content_hash alone, git is a convenience layered on top, never a dependency.

resulting_state_ref.description: An immutable identifier for resulting_state's own content at the moment this cycle completed -- resulting_state itself is a live path that LATER cycles go on to mutate, so without this, an OLD episode's own historical state is not reconstructable from the episode alone, only from archaeology entirely outside DEP. Optional: a cycle whose harness doesn't yet call blueprint.dep.state_ref simply omits it.

next_cycle_readiness.description: How the resulting state is discoverable without private agent memory (Gate 11).
